saml.description: Vault SAML configuration does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding validation flags are enabled.
saml.note: A successful forged or unsigned SAML login under this configuration is by documented default behavior, not necessarily an implementation bug.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the authenticated principal value.
saml.source: auth/token lookup-self sample response and Vault auth display naming conventions
saml.note: Do not flag mount-path prefixes as identity-collision bugs when the suffix matches the sent identity.

saml.description: Successful SAML login can create identity group aliases using values from the configured groups_attribute.
saml.note: Additional inherited policies via mapped identity groups are expected when group aliases are configured; this is by design and must be compared against upstream group intent and broker policy.

saml.description: Vault-issued tokens are reusable until TTL expiry when token_num_uses is 0.
saml.source: Token API and SAML role readback document token_num_uses 0 as unlimited uses.
saml.note: Repeated successful use of the same Vault token is by design unless a use limit or revocation condition was configured.

saml.description: SAML groups are represented through Identity group aliases derived from the configured groups_attribute rather than direct entity membership edits on login.
saml.source: SAML role docs: groups_attribute is used as the names for the Identity group aliases created due to a successful login.
saml.note: Absence of group-derived policies without a matching group alias is expected setup behavior, not necessarily an authorization bug.

saml.description: If no default_role is configured on the SAML auth method, a role must be provided during login flow initiation.
saml.source: SAML config docs: If default_role is not set, a role is required during login.
saml.note: A login failure without a role under this configuration is expected and should not be treated as a coherence or auth bypass issue.

saml.constraint: SAML config trust source selection: configure_jwt_validation MUST set either idp_metadata_url OR the full manual trust tuple (idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert). idp_metadata_url is mutually exclusive with the manual fields. For issuer-validation tests, if idp_entity_id is omitted in manual mode, setup is invalid because the API requires it.

SAML signature validation defaults are insecure-by-default for testing: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For F-2/F-7 insecure-default tests, leave them unset/false. For normal baseline/control logins and for I1 assertion-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly enable the relevant validation flags or login may succeed by design without verifying signatures.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion / saml_spurious_signature / saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests, configure_jwt_validation SHOULD enable validate_assertion_signature=true. Enabling only validate_response_signature checks at least the response envelope and may accept an unsigned assertion by design, which would misclassify response-level-only validation as a generic signature bypass.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution tests in manual configuration mode, idp_cert is the trust anchor used to verify response and assertion signatures. The fuzzer MUST keep idp_cert pinned to the intended trusted IdP certificate during attack logins; changing idp_cert to the attacker certificate is a setup change, not a bypass.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, issuer checking depends on configured IdP identity. In manual configuration mode, idp_entity_id is required and should be set to the trusted issuer; then send saml_login with idp_entity_id='https://wrong-issuer.example/idp'. If the trusted issuer is not configured, an issuer-mismatch result is uninterpretable.

SAML flow coherence: Vault SAML login is a 3-step flow bound by client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id: /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url -> /auth/{mount}/callback -> /auth/{mount}/token. The fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id and its matching client_verifier within the same sequence and MUST NOT mix values across concurrent flows, or failures are expected by design (I3).

ACS URL binding: the acs_url sent to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must be one of the configured acs_urls. For SAML tests, the executor MUST use a configured ACS URL exactly; otherwise callback/token completion failures are setup errors, not security findings.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type='string', values are exact matches only. If bound_subjects_type='glob', '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple different subjects to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type='glob' with an appropriate pattern; setting bound_subjects='*' without glob mode matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is 'string', which requires exact string matches; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple different attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or switch to glob mode with an appropriate pattern; setting an exact-match attribute value to '*' matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as a single string or a comma-separated list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric-like coercion by configuring a bound attribute value as an integer-like string N and sending a SAML attribute value like N+0.7 or alternate typed serialization if supported by the generator, to detect silent coercion/truncation rather than outright rejection.

groups_attribute is an exact attribute-name selector with no companion matching-mode parameter. It does not support wildcards. It selects which SAML attribute supplies external group names for alias creation. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, vary the attribute values, not the groups_attribute field name.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with the issued session token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both verification and access testing, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3 if an additional session-backed entity lookup is included.

Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role token fields: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses. token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than a literal immediate-expiry token. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means 'expire now' or 'deny all uses' for these fields.

Vault token lookup-self display and metadata are mount-derived. verify_granted_identity may return a display_name prefixed by the auth mount path rather than the raw asserted subject. I4 identity comparisons MUST use the configured prefix pattern oracle rather than exact string equality on display_name.

Identity group type semantics: create_identity_group supports type 'internal' or 'external'. For external identity-provider groups, membership is established via aliases rather than manual member_entity_ids. The fuzzer SHOULD use create_group_alias with groups_attribute-driven SAML group names instead of manually populating external group membership when testing I5 group policy propagation.

Group policy application mode can change authorization results across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy; if 'within_namespace_hierarchy', historical namespace restrictions apply. Cross-namespace I5 tests MUST account for this global mode or they may report false positives/negatives.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh assertion in the same configured role and flow. A failed replay attempt without a successful control cannot distinguish replay enforcement from broken SAML setup (bad ACS URL, bad verifier/poll binding, or invalid signature settings).

SAML auth config defaults are insecure for signature validation: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false by default. For I1 saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave them unset/false; to test hardened behavior, set validate_response_signature=true and validate_assertion_signature=true.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, configure_jwt_validation MUST set idp_entity_id when not using idp_metadata_url. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer trust comes from metadata; if manual IdP config is used and idp_entity_id is omitted, setup is invalid because idp_entity_id is required. Do NOT interpret acceptance under missing issuer configuration as a mismatch bypass unless the docs-supported default path actually omitted issuer validation.

SAML config has mutually exclusive trust-anchor modes: idp_metadata_url cannot be combined with idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, or idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one trust source. For attacker-cert substitution tests that need explicit attacker-controlled certs or issuer values, use manual mode (idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert), not metadata mode.

The SAML login flow is multi-step and session-bound: obtain /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url first to get token_poll_id and RelayState context, then POST the SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback, then exchange /auth/{mount}/token with the matching client_verifier and token_poll_id. A valid I3 test MUST preserve this exact flow coherence; mixing callback data or token_poll_id/client_verifier across flows will cause by-design failures.

The ACS URL used at login must be one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST configure configure_jwt_validation.acs_urls to include the exact callback URL it will use in the SAML flow; otherwise callback/login failures are setup errors, not security findings.

SAML role matching semantics: bound_subjects supports exact matching when bound_subjects_type=string and wildcard matching only when bound_subjects_type=glob. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different NameID/subject values must authenticate through the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' without bound_subjects_type=glob; in string mode it is a literal asterisk.

SAML role matching semantics: bound_attributes values are exact string matches by default because bound_attributes_type defaults to string. Wildcards are only interpreted when bound_attributes_type=glob. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple attribute values to pass, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with a deliberate pattern. Do NOT assume '*' is a wildcard in default mode.

SAML bound_attributes accepted value types are documented as string or comma-separated list of strings. There is no documentation for numeric/boolean cross-type coercion. For I5 type-coercion testing, the fuzzer SHOULD probe whether non-string SAML attribute values are coerced or rejected, but MUST treat outright rejection as expected unless evidence shows coercion. Unlike JWT bound_claims, there is no documented numeric mode toggle here.

token_num_uses on SAML roles limits total uses of the issued Vault token. Every API call made with that session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, consumes uses. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated verification call is included.
Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role token fields: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Do not treat 0 as 'deny all' or single-use.

Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role TTL fields from read_role_config: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than literal zero-second usable tokens. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume a returned 0 means immediate expiry; verify effective TTL via token lookup-self.

Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth-mount-derived prefix rather than the raw upstream identity. I4 tests MUST compare the granted display_name using the documented prefix pattern instead of exact equality with the sent identity.

Identity group type semantics matter for external group mapping. SAML groups_attribute is used as the names for Identity group aliases created due to successful login. For external IdP group mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD create external-style group mappings via create_group_alias and avoid relying on manual member_entity_ids assignment as proof of external group behavior.

Group policy application can be globally altered by /sys/config/group-policy-application. If the mode is set to 'any', group policies can apply across namespace boundaries; if 'within_namespace_hierarchy', historical namespace scoping applies. I5 group-policy-escalation tests MUST account for this global mode to avoid false positives about cross-namespace policy inheritance.

For I2 SAML replay tests, use a control login in the same configured flow to confirm the SAML setup is valid before interpreting a replay failure or success. A failed replay attempt without a successful baseline can be caused by broken SAML flow setup rather than replay protection.

SAML auth config trust source is exclusive: configure_jwt_validation MUST set either idp_metadata_url OR the explicit trio/idp fields (idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, idp_cert). idp_metadata_url is mutually exclusive with the explicit IdP settings. Tests that intend to control issuer or signing cert behavior MUST use explicit fields rather than metadata URL so the trust anchor is deterministic.

Vault SAML signature validation defaults are insecure for testing I1: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For normal positive-control setups, the fuzzer MUST explicitly enable the validation(s) it expects. For the documented insecure-default test, leave them unset/false on purpose; a successful forged SAML login in that configuration is testing the default, not a bypass of an enabled check.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and saml_issuer_mismatch tests, if idp_metadata_url is used, Vault derives trust material and issuer information from metadata. To test attacker-controlled certs or issuer mismatches precisely, the fuzzer SHOULD configure explicit idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, and idp_cert values instead of metadata URL, so the expected issuer and verification certificate are fixed and not auto-refreshed from metadata.

SAML role matching semantics: bound_subjects supports two modes controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, values are exact string matches only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' while leaving type unset/string; that matches only the literal '*'.

SAML attribute matching semantics: bound_attributes values are matched according to bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. With bound_attributes_type=string, values are exact string matches only; with glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need varying attribute values to pass, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with a deliberate pattern. Do NOT assume wildcards work under the default string mode.

SAML bound_attributes accepted value types are documented as single string or comma-separated list of strings. Non-string claim/attribute coercion behavior is not specified. For I5 type-coercion testing, the fuzzer SHOULD probe whether numeric-looking SAML attribute values are compared as raw strings only; do not assume integer/float coercion exists.

Vault token use-budget parameter token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued session token, and every authenticated API call consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret in the verify phase. If the fuzzer needs both self-lookup and a protected-resource read after login, token_num_uses MUST be at least 2; use at least 3 if any additional session-authenticated inspection call is included.

Numeric sentinel semantics for SAML role token fields: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than an immediately expired token. Never interpret 0 as literal zero lifetime or zero-use denial without checking the field's documented meaning.

For I2 SAML replay tests, the ACS callback (/auth/{mount}/callback) does not itself return the Vault token; the login flow is multi-step and session-bound through token_poll_id and client_verifier. A valid replay test must preserve the same SAML assertion semantics across callback submissions and then complete /auth/{mount}/token for each attempt. Do not treat callback success alone as authentication success.

For I3 flow-coherence tests on Vault SAML, the login flow is explicitly split across sso_service_url -> callback -> token. The fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id and its matching client_verifier paired within the same flow. Mixing a callback from one flow with a token exchange from another is an invalid setup and any failure is not evidence of a security property.

For I5 group-policy escalation tests, groups_attribute causes successful SAML logins to create/use Identity group aliases named from the asserted group values. To test group-derived authorization, the fuzzer MUST pre-create the internal identity group and matching group alias on the SAML mount accessor; otherwise missing group alias setup can make group-based policy grants appear absent for setup reasons rather than enforcement reasons.

Vault identity groups support type=internal or type=external. External groups are intended to represent external identity-provider groups and should be linked via aliases. For SAML group-mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use group aliases rather than manual member_entity_ids to model upstream group membership; otherwise the test may not exercise SAML group binding at all.

Global group policy application mode can affect I5 results across namespaces. Vault's /sys/config/group-policy-application defaults to within_namespace_hierarchy, while mode any applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests MUST account for this global mode; a policy grant across namespaces may be by design when mode=any.
